headline: Former Healey aide faces federal SNAP-fraud case while awaiting drug trial
dek: Lamar Cook is accused of hiding income and household information to receive food assistance; he was released after appearing in Boston federal court.
body: Federal prosecutors have charged Lamar Cook, a former Massachusetts state official from Springfield, with SNAP fraud and wire fraud, adding a federal case to the drug and firearm charges he was already facing in Hampden County. Cook, 46, was arrested Wednesday, Oct. 14, and appeared in federal court in Boston later that day, according to the [U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts](https://www.justice.gov/usao-ma/pr/former-massachusetts-state-official-charged-snap-fraud).

The new case centers on Cook’s April 6 application for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits. Federal prosecutors allege that he reported zero income, less than $100 in his bank account and a two-person household consisting of himself and his minor child. The criminal complaint says investigators found more than $8,800 in one of his accounts at the time and identified additional deposits, including about $12,000 in payments from his mother after she won roughly $1 million in the Massachusetts Lottery.

Prosecutors also allege that Cook did not disclose that his fiancée and her mother lived at his Springfield home, or that his fiancée earned more than $80,000 a year from Springfield Public Schools. The federal release says Cook received about $546 a month in SNAP benefits. Transaction records and retail surveillance allegedly show that the benefits were used at grocery and other stores in Massachusetts and during a July trip to Florida; the release says his fiancée was also observed using his electronic-benefit-transfer card for household purchases.

Cook’s appearance in federal court produced an immediate procedural development but not a decision on whether he committed the alleged fraud. [CBS Boston reported](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/lamar-cook-maura-healey-snap-fraud-arrest/) that he was released on personal recognizance after the arraignment. Federal prosecutors sought a temporary detention period so Hampden County prosecutors could ask to revoke his release in the older case. The [Boston Globe reported](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/14/metro/lamar-cook-arrest-snap-fraud-drug-trafficking-healey/) that state prosecutors requested a Thursday hearing on that issue.

The federal allegations are tied to Cook’s earlier role in state government. Governor Maura Healey appointed him in 2023 as deputy director of her Western Massachusetts office in Springfield. He was terminated in October 2025 after he was detained at the Springfield State Office Building and later charged in Hampden County with alleged trafficking of more than 200 grams of cocaine, conspiracy and firearm offenses. Cook has pleaded not guilty in that case, and those charges remain unresolved.

The federal release says Cook’s state salary was $130,227 and that he later received $22,374.29 in net pay for accrued vacation leave after his termination. The Commonwealth said it recognized an error and tried to reverse the direct deposits but could not recover the money because there were insufficient funds in his accounts, according to the release. The Globe reported that Healey’s administration separately sued in January to recover more than $31,000 in vacation-pay funds; that civil dispute is still pending.

The case also puts attention on how SNAP eligibility is checked in Massachusetts. SNAP is a federal program administered in the state through the Department of Transitional Assistance, and applicants must report the income and household circumstances used to determine eligibility. The federal complaint alleges that Cook’s financial information and household composition were materially different from what he reported. Those claims have not been tested at trial, and the charging document does not establish that other applicants or the broader benefits system were affected.

If convicted, the SNAP-fraud count carries a statutory maximum of five years in prison, while the wire-fraud count carries a maximum of 20 years, along with potential fines and supervised release, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said. Those are legal maximums, not a prediction of a sentence. Cook is presumed innocent unless prosecutors prove the charges beyond a reasonable doubt. The next immediate question is whether Hampden County prosecutors succeed in changing his state-court release conditions while the federal case proceeds; the defense has not publicly addressed the new allegations in the reports reviewed for this story.
author: NorthEast News Desk

seoDescription: Former Massachusetts official Lamar Cook faces SNAP-fraud and wire-fraud charges while awaiting a separate drug and firearm case in Hampden County.
